content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text evaluates D5 vs C5 on Isaiah 7:14 by noting that CR2 G answers the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows but leaves the sign's sense open, which is a verse-by-verse/underdetermination treatment of the pressed link rather than chain-against-chain footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"the phrase 'the pressing side's own chain read together': I weighed whether the judge's reference to 'rows' treats the challenger's rows as a chain read together (so K-C applies) or as isolated rows (so K-C would not apply).","why":"The judge leaves the link underdetermined because the sign's sense is open after the rows are answered, which is the retired stating-verse/verse-by-verse approach rather than weighing chain against chain by footing."}
